cells.reason: The passages describe multiple overall changes at Merrill since the start of 2026 (recruiting strategy, new fees, new services, settlements, financial metrics), each captured as a fact item.

items.text: Merrill returned to veteran broker recruiting in 2026 after largely pulling back at the end of 2017, restoring a focus on hiring and a more aggressive offer under Co-Presidents Lindsay Hans and Eric Schimpf, who took over in 2023.
items.quote: Merrill executives in October touted that recruited assets to the wealth unit doubled year-over-year as the firm has returned to veteran broker recruiting. The firm largely pulled back from veteran broker recruiting at the end of 2017 but returned after Co-Presidents Lindsay Hans and Eric Schimpf, who took over in 2023, restored a focus on hiring and a more aggressive offer.

items.text: Merrill executives in October 2026 touted that recruited assets to the wealth unit doubled year-over-year as the firm returned to veteran broker recruiting.
items.quote: Merrill executives in October touted that recruited assets to the wealth unit doubled year-over-year as the firm has returned to veteran broker recruiting.

items.text: Merrill's parent Bank of America reportedly saw the largest net losses among advisors this year through Aug. 13, with a net loss of 552 advisors, according to Wolfe Research.
items.quote: Bank of America had a net loss of 552 advisors, followed by Edward Jones and Equitable Advisors, with 334 each.

items.text: Merrill created new 'data analytics' and revenue-sharing 'support' fees for third-party asset managers, effective Jan. 1, 2027, offering those who pay greater visibility and 'recommendation' from brokers.
items.quote: Two kinds of fees have been newly created. Third-party managers can buy as much as $1.4 million worth of "incentives" per annum through one fee, by maxing out data analytics buys... And the Bank of America subsidiary is making it possible to pay more to get more visibility and middleman love, effective, Jan. 1, 2027.

items.text: Merrill's new data analytics fees will cost asset managers between $125,000 and $860,000 per firm per year for data on actively managed products.
items.quote: Merrill's new data analytics fees will cost asset managers between $125,000 and $860,000 per-firm, per-year for data on actively managed products, including ETFs, mutual funds, annuities and model portfolios.

items.text: Merrill's new 'negotiable' revenue-sharing 'support fee' can cost up to $1 million for every $1 billion of funds an asset manager manages, with rates up to 0.1% (10 basis points).
items.quote: Its new "negotiable" revenue-sharing "support fee" will cost up to $1 million, for every $1 billion of funds an asset manager manages on behalf of Merrill advisors, with fees ranging from 0.02% on high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth assets, to a maximum 0.1% on third party mutual funds, money market funds, and active ETFs.

items.text: Merrill launched two new services in September 2026, Tax Efficient Transition Service (TET) and Dollar Cost Averaging Service (DCA), to support tax-efficient portfolio transitions and systematic cash investing.
items.quote: Merrill today announced the launch of Tax Efficient Transition Service (TET) and Dollar Cost Averaging Service (DCA), new services that combine automation with professional portfolio oversight to help clients simplify asset transitions and cash deployment.

items.text: Merrill agreed to a settlement with state securities regulators over charges of unreasonable commissions on small-dollar retail equity transactions, with restitution of approximately $549,000 in excess commissions.
items.quote: Merrill Lynch faces restitution on approximately $549,000 in excess commissions over the same period, NASAA said.

items.text: Merrill agreed to pay $39 million to settle a class action lawsuit alleging it paid brokerage clients close-to-zero interest rates instead of market rates on cash in retirement accounts.
items.quote: the Thundering Herd agreeing this week to pay $39 million to settle a class action lawsuit that alleged it paid brokerage clients close-to-zero interest rates instead of market rates on cash in retirement accounts.

items.text: Merrill client sales of alternative investments increased 19% in the third quarter of 2026, according to Eric Schimpf, president and co-head of Merrill Wealth Management.
items.quote: At Merrill Lynch, client sales of alternative investments increased 19% in the quarter, said Eric Schimpf, president and co-head of Merrill Wealth Management.

items.text: Merrill client balances were $4.2 trillion in the third quarter of 2026, up 9% year-over-year.
Merrill added about 4,200 net new households with at least $500,000 in assets in the third quarter of 2026, up 17%.
items.quote: Merrill added about 4,200 net new households with at least $500,000 in assets, up 17%.
